subject: Reserved Capacity: tiered trigger clauses & GPU spot-price pass-through
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Park <hannah@aurora.ai>, procurement@aurora.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal + pass-through trigger language

Hannah / team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is an initial reserved capacity offer that maps to the Aurora usage profile you shared (see RDW_Aurora_Reserved_Offer_v1.pdf). A couple of notes up front:

- We matched the SKU mix to your expected inference mix (small-medium-high token tiers) and included a 12-month and 24-month price option.
- Pricing sensitivity: because a meaningful portion of our unit cost for the dedicated fleet depends on spot GPU market shifts, we included a proposed "price-trigger" clause that relaxes the guaranteed discount if the underlying GPU index moves beyond agreed thresholds.

I wanted to call out the proposed mechanism so we can confirm whether Aurora will accept a limited pass-through vs. requiring fixed unit pricing for the full term. The attachment pricing-sensitivity-matrix.xlsx shows breakpoints and the modeled <5/15/30% passthrough exposure.

Ask: can you confirm procurement's tolerance for a trigger-based clause vs. a fixed price with a larger up-front commitment? If you prefer, we can propose a capped escalation or a quarterly review cadence.

I've cc'd Marissa for account-level details and Laura for finance visibility. If this looks generally acceptable, next step is a short redline of the contract language — I attached a quick draft to start that conversation.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDW_Aurora_Reserved_Offer_v1.pdf (pdf), pricing-sensitivity-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), proposed-contract-clause-draft.txt (txt)

From: Hannah Park <hannah@aurora.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aurora.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal + pass-through trigger language

Karthik —

Thanks for the materials. Quick initial reactions from procurement: we can accept a trigger-style approach in principle, but we need clarity on three items before moving to legal review:

1) Definition of the GPU index and the source (public exchange or vendor-provided).
2) Clear cap on total pass-through exposure over any 12-month window.
3) A mitigation/discount if Aurora commits to expanding seat count mid-term (we'd expect upside protection if we grow).

Also, our CFO prefers language that ties any escalation to a publicly auditable index vs. a vendor-provided internal metric. Can you confirm what index Redwood is planning to reference?

Please keep Marissa and Laura on the thread; we'll share an internal procurement note after our call later today.

Best,
Hannah Park
Head of Procurement, Aurora AI

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Park <hannah@aurora.ai>, procurement@aurora.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity proposal + pass-through trigger language

Hannah —

Appreciate the clear feedback. To address your three bullets, here is a practical proposal that we think balances predictability and market reality:

1) Index: reference the GPU Spot Index maintained by the public exchange (we use the Bloomberg GPU Spot Index by default) or alternatively, the monthly weighted-average price reported by two major cloud GPU markets (we can list these explicitly in the contract). We'll include the exact formula in the contract appendix so it's auditable.

2) Cap: pass-through is capped at 8% in any rolling 12-month period for the 12-month term, and 6% for a 24-month term. Above that cap, Redwood covers excess volatility. The pricing-sensitivity-matrix.xlsx attached shows example scenarios.

3) Growth protection: if Aurora expands committed capacity by >25% during the term, we will apply a 1.5% growth discount on incremental units and reset the pass-through cap on the incremental tranche.

Contract language (excerpt) included in proposed-contract-clause-draft.txt: "In the event the GPU Spot Index increases by more than X% relative to the contract baseline, Customer and Redwood agree to a pass-through adjustment up to the cap defined in Appendix B. Any adjustment will be calculated monthly and subject to the 12-month rolling cap."

Next steps: Laura — can you run the modeled cashflows for both 12- and 24-month options and confirm the net present value impact at the caps above? If the numbers look OK we can surface to Ben for an approval to accept the 24-month at the 6% cap (that would be my ask given Aurora's growth signals).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-sensitivity-matrix.xlsx, proposed-contract-clause-draft.txt

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Reserved capacity proposal + pass-through trigger language — finance check + approval request

Marissa / Karthik —

Ran the cashflow delta for both terms using the caps you suggested. Key points:

- 12-month term (8% rolling cap): NPV impact vs. fixed-price baseline = -$210k (i.e., Redwood downside if market moves favorably is lower; upside risk limited by cap).
- 24-month term (6% rolling cap): NPV impact = -$320k but gives better retention and higher ARR predictability.

Given Aurora's stated growth signals and the referenced HubSpot usage trend, I'm supportive of offering the 24-month at the 6% cap, provided we get Ben's approval for the incremental revenue-at-risk. If we want to tighten risk even more, we can propose a quarterly reset with a 90-day lookback to smooth spikes.

Ben — can you sign off on approving the 24-month option with the 6% rolling cap and the growth discount (1.5% on incremental units) as Marissa outlined? This would be within our delegated approval band if you confirm. If you prefer, we can surface to exec review for anything above 8% exposure.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — Revenue Ops
